units.normalized_content: Repository title: Dostoevskian Cybernetics; subtitle frames causal error attribution for efficient structural adaptation under environmental shift.
Prediction error alone is not enough for efficient adaptation; systems may benefit from identifying which internal mechanism produced an error before structural change.
Optimize the process generating corrections, not merely corrections; seek minimum sufficient structural change for future viability while retaining ability to recognize unjustified revision.
Dostoevskian Cybernetics treats contradiction as information about the process producing a conclusion and distinguishes observation, assumption, mechanism, representation, and interface failure loci.
Recursive Error Metabolism asks what failed, why, what smallest revision is required, and whether the failure is identifiable.
CFAE is a diagnostic routing layer evaluating competing failure hypotheses before allowing structural updates.
Factored Shock Benchmark is proposed to test causal attribution under controlled shifts including noise, compound failures, deceptive correlations, and non-identifiable interfaces.
A_epistemic and C_improve are proposed to measure validity and efficiency of structural adaptation, not only performance recovery.
Observation failure: test whether perception/data/noise caused the contradiction; response may adjust/filter observation representation.
Inference failure: test whether reasoning/evidence/stochastic anomaly explains the contradiction; accumulate evidence before structural revision.
Mechanism failure: test whether causal dynamics changed; revise the isolated mechanism while preserving unaffected components.
Representation failure: test whether variables/abstractions omit needed distinctions; expand or revise causal representation.
Interface failure: test whether the target is identifiable from available information; if not, halt revision, preserve provenance and competing hypotheses, and signal an epistemic limit.
Interface sufficiency is represented by L = L_hat ∘ O; failure motivates epistemic halt rather than forced structural revision.
A_epistemic = (Correct Attribution + Correct Abstention) / Total Contradictions.
C_improve = ΔP_future / (ΔI_necessary + λ ΔI_unnecessary) × A_epistemic.
ΔP_future denotes future performance recovery; ΔI_necessary justified structural change; ΔI_unnecessary churn from noise/incorrect attribution/unidentifiable causes; λ penalizes unnecessary churn.
Agent A: Monolithic; no attribution; baseline without decomposition.
Agent B: Factored with global update; tests whether modularity alone is sufficient.
Agent E: Factored with random attribution; tests whether attribution accuracy matters.
Agent C: Factored + CFAE causal diagnosis; proposed mechanism.
Agent D: Factored + Oracle perfect attribution; upper bound.
clean_shock: single-factor identifiable shifts; tests localization.
stochastic_noise: transient anomalies; tests resistance to premature revision.
compound_failure: multiple simultaneous failures; tests escalation beyond single-factor attribution.
deceptive_correlation: spurious correlations; tests recognition of representation failure.
interface_wall: non-identifiable environments; tests epistemic-limit recognition.

units.normalized_content: Repository explicitly states it contains a proposed framework and experimental program.
Central source hypothesis: efficient adaptation requires learning from errors plus identification of the process that generated the error before changing the system.
Benchmark purpose is to determine where the hypothesis holds, where it fails, and what limits exist; no result is claimed here.
Prediction error indicates contradiction but does not identify which internal assumption generated it; detection and causal attribution are separate problems.
